    A Ghost in Your Ear

    5:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Most days Going out

    When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.

    Natalie Brooke & Matt Jalbert Band

    6:30 PM · Bowery Palace, East Village · $31.90 Going out

    Natalie Brooke is a rock star. A virtuoso funk / rock keys player leading her powerhouse 4-piece band from the Baltimore area. The explosive act is fronted by Natalie on keys, synth, keytar, and vocals and backed by drummer Nathan Shulkin, Nester on the bass, and Luke Walker on the guitar. She kicks off every show with a punch and never lets the energy drop - audiences move, dance, scream, jump, and ride the wild wave of the set with her and the band. Natalie's music was once said to be a mashup of Rick James and Rush. She has an undeniably infectious vibe featuring a fiery blend of fast tempos and sloshy rock elements balanced with her transcendent jazz and classical roots. Natalie brings an exceptionally unique approach to the keyboard that is equally percussive and melodic that lights up the show with every electrifying note she plays. She is on a meteoric rise, frequently sharing the stage with pillars of the rock, funk, and jazz scenes. Pigeons Playing Ping Pong, Andy Frasco & the UN, Dogs in a Pile, Kanika Moore, Big Something, Cris Jacobs, Doom Flamingo, Sunsquabi, lespecial, and the Magic Beans are a few of the artists Natalie has played with recently. Matt Jalbert Band is the new song-driven project from guitarist and founding member of TAUK. After more than a decade of touring nationally with TAUK---including appearances at Bonnaroo and Hulaween and performances at venues like Red Rocks Amphitheatre---Jalbert steps forward as a lead vocalist and songwriter, bringing a new dimension to his sound. Blending groove-forward indie rock with psychedelic and blues influences, Matt Jalbert Band pairs deep-pocket grooves and adventurous musicianship with concise, melodic, and lyrical songs. The lineup features Matt Jalbert (guitar/vocals), Ben Atkind (drums), Eli Winderman (keys/vocals), Jonathan Colman (bass), and Adam November (guitar). The album, Somebody's Child, arrives November 20, with the title track and first single dropping September 18. Following Jalbert's 2025 instrumental solo release Sauce Buffet, Somebody's Child marks a new chapter---pairing his signature guitar work and groove with vocals, melody, and a more direct emotional voice.

    Senri Oe Trio

    7:00 PM · Birdland Theater, Hell's Kitchen · $35.46 Something special

    Halloween night at Birdland. Expect the unexpected. On the most magical night of the year, something extraordinary is about to happen at New York City's legendary Birdland Theater. The music will cast its own spell --- and once it does, you won't want to break free. Senri Oe Trio takes the stage for two extraordinary nights --- four sets of music that defy category, blur boundaries, and just might bewitch you. Senri Oe is one of the most remarkable reinventions in contemporary music. Beginning classical piano at age three and discovering jazz at fifteen, he first rose to extraordinary heights in Japan: a multi-platinum recording artist, Japanese Grammy winner, actor, television anchor, and author --- a cultural icon whose name defined an era. At forty-seven, at the peak of his fame, Senri made a bold and deeply personal choice. He walked away from stardom, moved to New York City with his beloved dachshund, Peace, and enrolled in The New School for Jazz and Contemporary Music. Under the mentorship of masters including Junior Mance and Aaron Goldberg, he reinvented himself from scratch. It was not a retreat. It was a return to his first love. Since his 2012 jazz debut, Boys Mature Slow, Senri has built a powerful international presence --- performing at the Atlanta and Detroit Jazz Festivals, headlining SummerFest for two consecutive years, and charting at #24 on JazzWeek in 2023 with his album Class of '88. These Birdland performances celebrate the worldwide release of his latest album, HOMEWORK (Global release: September 4, 2026) --- conceived in his Brooklyn living room and recorded at The Bunker Studio with bassist Matt Clohesy and drummer Ross Pederson, with mixing by Aaron Nevezie. HOMEWORK fuses digital and acoustic worlds into a soundtrack without visuals: brilliant, edgy, and profoundly human. Don't miss your chance to be part of something unforgettable. This Halloween, let the music haunt you.

    Pasquale Grasso Trio

    5:30 PM · Birdland Jazz Club, Hell's Kitchen · $35.46 · ↻ Every Saturday Something special

    It was the kind of endorsement most rising guitarists can only dream of, and then some. In his interview for Vintage Guitar magazines February 2016 cover story, Pat Metheny was asked to name some younger musicians whod impressed him. The best guitar player Ive heard in maybe my entire life is floating around now, Pasquale Grasso, said the jazz-guitar icon and NEA Jazz Master. This guy is doing something so amazingly musical and so difficult.Mostly what I hear now are guitar players who sound a little bit like me mixed with a little bit of [John Scofield] and a little bit of [Bill Frisell], he continued. Whats interesting about Pasquale is that he doesnt sound anything like that at all. In a way, it is a little bit of a throwback, because his modelwhich is an incredible model to haveis Bud Powell. He has somehow captured the essence of that language from piano onto guitar in a way that almost nobody has ever addressed. Hes the most significant new guy Ive heard in many, many years.As hes done with many rising jazz stars, Metheny later invited Grasso over to his New York pad to jam and share some wisdom. Hes since become a generous presence in Grassos life, and his assessment of Grassos playing isno surprisespot-on. Born in Italy and now based in New York City, the 30-year- old guitarist has developed an astounding technique and concept informed not by jazz guitarists so much as by bebop pioneers like Powell, Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie and the classical-guitar tradition. His new digital-only EP series, available beginning in June from Sony Masterworks, showcases Grasso in the solo-guitar format, where his intensive studies of both midcentury jazz and classical meld into a signature mastery that is, remarkably, at once unprecedented and evocative.

Featuring guitarist Nick Cassarino, bassist Nate Edgar and drummer Nikki Glaspie, the seasoned trio delivers a transcendent blend of soul, funk, rock and rhythm and blues. Multi-part vocal harmonies and elevated musicianship inspires audiences to dance, groove, make love or just stand there with goose bumps. The Nth Powers electric live performances have been flooring audiences ever since the group first aligned in New Orleans during Jazz Fest. After the bands breakout 2013 EP, Basic Minimum Skills Test, The Nth Power went on to release two acclaimed studio albums and two live albums garnering national coverage in Relix, Modern Drummer, Huffington Post, Glide, Consequence, Okayplayer, Paste and Sirius XM Radio.The trios individual music credentials include collaborating with artists like Beyonce, Snarky Puppy, Maceo Parker, Dumpstaphunk, Big Daddy Kane and John Browns Body. Its my dream team, said bandleader and drummer Glaspie. Each one of us is a songwriter, so when we get together, everything becomes that much stronger. Were going as far as you can go on the planet Earth and playing music. The Nth Powers inspirational sets have floored audiences at music festivals like Electric Forest, High Sierra, Peachfest, North Coast Music Festival and Hulaween. They maintain New Orleans as their spiritual home, and the celebratory essence of that citys music culture is palpable in each performance. Simply put, there is something pretty magical happening in this band, and theyre only just getting started. Please Note: All Sales Final.

    Senri Oe Trio

    7:00 PM · Birdland Theater, Hell's Kitchen · $35.46 Something special

    Halloween night at Birdland. Expect the unexpected. On the most magical night of the year, something extraordinary is about to happen at New York City's legendary Birdland Theater. The music will cast its own spell --- and once it does, you won't want to break free. Senri Oe Trio takes the stage for two extraordinary nights --- four sets of music that defy category, blur boundaries, and just might bewitch you. Senri Oe is one of the most remarkable reinventions in contemporary music. Beginning classical piano at age three and discovering jazz at fifteen, he first rose to extraordinary heights in Japan: a multi-platinum recording artist, Japanese Grammy winner, actor, television anchor, and author --- a cultural icon whose name defined an era. At forty-seven, at the peak of his fame, Senri made a bold and deeply personal choice. He walked away from stardom, moved to New York City with his beloved dachshund, Peace, and enrolled in The New School for Jazz and Contemporary Music. Under the mentorship of masters including Junior Mance and Aaron Goldberg, he reinvented himself from scratch. It was not a retreat. It was a return to his first love. Since his 2012 jazz debut, Boys Mature Slow, Senri has built a powerful international presence --- performing at the Atlanta and Detroit Jazz Festivals, headlining SummerFest for two consecutive years, and charting at #24 on JazzWeek in 2023 with his album Class of '88. These Birdland performances celebrate the worldwide release of his latest album, HOMEWORK (Global release: September 4, 2026) --- conceived in his Brooklyn living room and recorded at The Bunker Studio with bassist Matt Clohesy and drummer Ross Pederson, with mixing by Aaron Nevezie. HOMEWORK fuses digital and acoustic worlds into a soundtrack without visuals: brilliant, edgy, and profoundly human. Don't miss your chance to be part of something unforgettable. This Halloween, let the music haunt you.

They really know their way around the business. Tables and seats are limited. Make early purchases. Ticket availability are unpredictable. Walk-ins possible, not guaranteed NOTES DRESS TO IMPRESS --- It's the Jazz Age! Play the part and feel the spirit of the space with cocktail or period attire. Leave jeans, shorts, no t-shirts unless accompanied by a collar or jacket. Leave hoodies at home. NO Athletic Wear, Undershirts , hoodies in THE ROOM Purchase HARD TICKETS for others as gifts. Will call is NOT transferable, NO REFUNDS (no exceptions) ID is required NO PETS allowed or shopping-bags and backpacks in THE ROOM. BYOBB (bring your own brown bag).

    A Ghost in Your Ear

    3:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Also on other days Going out

    When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.

    Sam Dillon Quintet

    5:30 PM · Birdland Jazz Club, Hell's Kitchen · $35.46 Something special

    Native New Yorker, saxophonist, composer and teacher, Sam Dillon has established himself as one of the most in demand musicians of his generation. Sam's prolific soloist and sideman work includes over 40 studio recordings, performances on a global level and international critical acclaim garnering him recognition as one of the defining voices on tenor saxophone today. In addition to Sam's work with The Jimmy Heath Big Band, Mingus Big Band, Slide Hampton Octet, The 8BitBigBand, The Steven Feifke Big Band, The Birdland Big Big and many others, Sam regularly leads his own quartet and has 4 albums out as a leader/co-leader to date. In 2016 Sam was awarded the Artist Diploma from The Juilliard School granting him his third degree in music performance including a masters degree from SUNY Purchase College in 2009. In 2013, Sam was selected as one of 13 semi-finalists in the Thelonious Monk International Jazz Saxophone Competition where he performed at the Smithsonian Institute in Washington D.C. Sam is very proud to be the director of the jazz program at USDAN Summer Camp For The Arts where he has acted as both a teacher and administrator for the past 5 years. Sam is an endorsing artist for Yamaha Saxophones and D'Addario Reeds. For more information please visit www.samdillonmusic.com.

    Michael Blake Quartet: Halloween Tales

    7:00 PM · Birdland Theater, Hell's Kitchen · $35.46 Something special

    New York saxophonist Michael Blake stakes out fresh territory in holiday jazz with Halloween Tales, out September 25, 2026. While the genre has typically belonged to the winter holidays, Blakes new release claims the mystery, humor and cinematic atmosphere of Halloween and the harvest season instead, channeled through inventive arrangements and inspired improvisation. Joined by Gary Versace on piano, Ben Allison on bass and Michael Sarin on drums, Blake leads a classic quartet lineup as a deliberate choice meant to echo the instrumentation of the holiday jazz records that shaped his own listening.

    ALEGRIA HALLOWEEN WEEKEND 2026 / ALEGRIA + VIVAALEGRIA HALLOWEEN WEEKEND NYC 2026 Halloween falls on a Saturday this year, and ALEGRIA is ready to celebrate with the return of one of our biggest and most anticipated weekends of the year! Join us on Saturday, October 31st --- Halloween Night --- for ALEGRIA HALLOWEEN, followed by VIVA Afterhours on Sunday morning, November 1st. Two back-to-back events, four incredible DJs and 16 hours of nonstop music celebrating Halloween in New York City. For more than two decades, ALEGRIA HALLOWEEN has become a NYC tradition, known for its incredible costumes, spectacular production and a packed dance floor that makes Halloween one of our favorite ALEGRIA nights of the year. ALEGRIA HALLOWEEN takes over Palladium Times Square on Saturday night from 10PM to 6AM, featuring Alberto Ponzo and Leanh. Then, just a few minutes away, the celebration continues at Harbor NYC with VIVA Afterhours from 6AM to 2PM on Sunday, featuring Rob Phillips and Jerac. 2-Event Passes for ALEGRIA + VIVA are also be available. If you're planning to attend both events, the 2-Event Pass is the best option, giving you express check-in at VIVA while paying only one ticketing fee for both events.
